Antworten & Erwähnungen

` (German overrides epics' English wording per project convention — same pattern Story 2.2 used). Reconciliation of "article footer" to `_partials/widgets/webmentions.html` mounted at end of article column follows Story 2.3's `head.html`-vs-`baseof.html` reconciliation pattern.

Webmentions grouped by type into four named sub-sections: Replies, Reposts, Mentions, Likes (in that visual order). Data shape from Story 3.2's `data/webmentions_by_article.json` (canonical schema in `digital-garden-integration-architecture.md` lines 871-902): each entry has `type` field with values `reply | repost | like | mention`. Partial groups via `where $mentions "type" "X"`, renders one `<section class="webmentions__group webmentions__group--{{ type }}">` per non-empty group with localized heading + count badge (`Antworten (3)`). Empty groups skipped. Type-to-heading mapping hardcoded (no i18n file in project).

Each entry shows: author name (always), avatar (only when `.author_photo` truthy — `{{ with .author_photo }}` skips empty/missing), reply text (only for `type == "reply"`), source link with date (always). Render `
` containing `` (no broken `` or placeholder for missing avatars), author `` with `rel="noopener external" target="_blank"`, optional `

`, source `` with `` formatted via Hugo's `dateFormat ":date_long"` (matching existing single.html lines 87-91 date style; site `languageCode: de` produces e.g. `15. November 2025`).

Webmentions load from `data/webmentions_by_article.json` (generated daily by Story 3.2). Hugo template uses graceful fallback per Critical Agent Rule #6 ("ALWAYS use `| default` when accessing data files"): `{{- $mentions := index .Site.Data.webmentions_by_article .RelPermalink | default (slice) -}}`. Missing data file (typical until Story 3.2 lands), missing key, or empty array all resolve to empty slice → AC #5 empty-state renders without erroring. NO HTTP fetch in browser — server-side rendered at build time from static JSON file (JAMstack on GitHub Pages, all engagement data via `.Site.Data.*` per architecture lines 296-308).

If no webmentions, section shows empty-state: `Noch keine Antworten. Sende einen Webmention!` (German, matches site convention). Implementation: when `len $mentions == 0`, render `

Noch keine Antworten. Sende einen Webmention!

` in place of grouped sections. Heading `

Antworten & Erwähnungen

` is STILL rendered (stable page structure across articles for crawlers/screen-readers). Optional inline `
` or link to Privacy Policy `## Webmentions` section (added by Story 2.3) — minimum viable: literal sentence.

External links open in new tab with `rel="noopener"` (and `rel="external"`, `target="_blank"`). Applies to: author profile link, source link, and any link inside reply content. Hugo's `safeHTML` does NOT auto-add these — must be in template literal HTML. Verification: `grep` rendered article page for `<a` inside `class="webmention"` and confirm each has `rel="noopener external"`. Combined with architecture line 1062 XSS protection, prevents both reverse-tabnabbing and XSS via webmention sender content.

Webmention count displayed below article title (e.g., "3 Antworten"). Implementation: in `single.html` `
` (lines 60-64), insert after subtitle `

` (line 62) and before `{{ .Content }}` (line 63): `{{- $mentions := index .Site.Data.webmentions_by_article .RelPermalink | default (slice) -}}` + gated `{{- if gt (len $mentions) 0 }}

N Antwort/Antworten

{{- end }}`. Anchor `#webmentions` targets the section id from AC #1. German pluralization: `1 Antwort` vs `N Antworten`. When zero webmentions, count line is NOT rendered (avoids meaningless "0 Antworten").

XSS protection for webmention reply content (derived from architecture line 1062 + ASR-003 `test-design-system.md` line 152). Reply `content` field comes from third-party senders via webmention.io and is potentially attacker-controlled. **Decision: option (a) — Hugo's default auto-escape; treat content as plain text.** Template uses `{{ .content }}` (auto-escaped), NOT `{{ .content | safeHTML }}`. HTML in source renders as literal text (`<script>` etc.). Story 3.2's `process-webmentions.js` is the right place for HTML sanitization (server-side, with `sanitize-html` allow-list); template-level auto-escape is the bulletproof default for Phase 1A.

Mock fixture file for development (per epics-md "Implementation Note (Mock Data)" line 326). Until Story 3.2 lands, `data/webmentions_by_article.json` does not exist. Create fixture covering all four type-groups. **Time-boxed exception to Critical Agent Rule #3** ("NEVER commit data/*.json to main"). Cleanup strategy: (a) rename to `.example.json` on merge (Hugo ignores `.example` extension) — RECOMMENDED; (b) delete after visual verification; (c) add `.gitignore` rule for `data/*.json` keeping local file for dev. Fixture content: 5 entries (2 replies, 1 like, 1 repost, 1 mention) keyed by a real article permalink with trailing slash.

No regression to existing single-page layouts. Diff `public/articles/<existing-post>/index.html` before/after — only the new webmention count line in `box-content`, the new `<section id="webmentions">` block at article footer (AC #1), and SCSS bundle hash should differ. Existing card variants (`.is-horizontal`, `.is-log`, `.has-image`), info widget (lines 76-131), TOC widget (lines 134-144), series widget (lines 146-175), related widget (lines 178-193), author widget (lines 196-214) render byte-equivalent. Critical Agent Rule #1 enforced: webmention display is purely additive.

Build still succeeds cleanly. `hugo --quiet --environment production --minify` exits 0 with no template-execution errors, no missing-variable warnings, no unresolved partial references. New partial, SCSS file, fixture data file all integrate without breaking existing build. Edge cases verified: (a) build with fixture present → AC #2 grouping renders; (b) build with fixture absent → AC #5 empty-state renders for all articles; (c) build for article NOT in fixture → AC #5 empty-state for that article only; (d) malformed fixture → either clean build error OR partial gracefully skips malformed entry — document chosen behavior.

doc.title: Functional Requirements
doc.section: FR-012 Webmention Display (lines 92-96); FR-011 Webmention Reception (lines 86-90 — reception only, owned by Story 2.3)
doc.snippet: FR-012: "Webmentions grouped by type and displayed in article footer." Validation: webmentions visible to readers, grouped by type. FR-011 (reception) is Story 2.3's scope and must precede this story for production data to flow; this story consumes the data file produced by Story 3.2.

doc.title: Integration Architecture — Hugo Data File Integration
doc.section: Hugo Data File Integration (lines 296-308); Daily Rebuild Data Flow (lines 250-294)
doc.snippet: Canonical pattern: `.Site.Data.<filename>` lookup; data files generated by daily GitHub Actions workflow on `data-updates` branch, merged into build workspace. Webmentions flow: webmention.io → fetch (Story 3.2) → `data/webmentions_raw.json` → process → `data/webmentions_by_article.json` → consumer (this story). Cache invalidation = next daily rebuild; webmentions are at most ~24h stale (acceptable for digital garden).

doc.title: Integration Architecture — webmentions_by_article.json schema
doc.snippet: Canonical schema. Top level: object keyed by article permalink (with trailing slash, e.g. `/articles/my-post/`); value is array of entries. Per-entry fields: `type` (`like|reply|repost|mention`), `author` (string), `author_url` (string), `author_photo` (string, optional/empty), `content` (string, replies only), `url` (string, source link), `published` (ISO 8601 timestamp). This story's partial template assumes this exact shape.

doc.title: Integration Architecture — Pattern 2: Dual Anonymous Engagement System
doc.snippet: Engagement infrastructure has two halves: hearts (proprietary, server-side aggregated via Umami — Stories 2.2, 3.1) and webmentions (federated, IndieWeb — Stories 2.3, 2.4, 3.2). Webmentions are the federated half. Both consume `.Site.Data.*` lookups in Hugo templates. This story renders the federated half on article pages.

doc.title: Integration Architecture — Critical Agent Rules + XSS protection
doc.snippet: Critical rules applicable to this story: #1 NEVER modify card variants (additive only); #3 NEVER commit data/*.json to main (deliberate exception in AC #9 for fixture); #5 NEVER use jQuery (this story has zero JS); #6 ALWAYS use `| default` on data lookups (strictly followed in both partial and count-line lookup). Line 1062: "XSS protection: Hugo templates auto-escape by default, manual HTML sanitization for webmention content" — this story takes the auto-escape default and defers sanitization to Story 3.2.

doc.title: Integration Architecture — Project Structure: webmentions.scss / webmentions.html designations
doc.snippet: Architecture explicitly designates new files: `assets/scss/elements/webmentions.scss` for styling and `_partials/webmentions.html` for the partial. This story reconciles the architecture's flat `_partials/webmentions.html` to project convention `_partials/widgets/webmentions.html` (siblings: `series.html`, `pagination.html`, `archive.html`, Story 2.2's `heart-button.html`) — same reconciliation Story 2.2 made for `heart-button.html`.

doc.title: System-Level Test Design — ASR-003 XSS Prevention
doc.snippet: ASR-003 (Score 6) XSS Prevention test approach: Playwright injection attempts against webmention content (``, ``). E2E spec at line 305 mentions webmentions display Playwright spec. Optional in this story since Hugo's auto-escape is correct by construction.

Establishes webmention.io account verification, `<link rel="webmention">` discovery in head.html, GitHub Secret `WEBMENTION_IO_TOKEN`, German `## Webmentions` section in `content/pages/datenschutz.md`, and CSP `connectsrc` allowance for `https://webmention.io` (already present in `_default/params.yaml` line 29 from Phase 0 Task 4.0). doc.title: Technical Architecture (PRD)
doc.snippet: Engagement infrastructure: webmention.io is canonical IndieWeb federated webmention receiver. JAMstack on GitHub Pages = no server runtime, so server-side rendering at build time is the only viable display strategy. Real-time webmentions out of architectural scope; daily rebuild cycle acceptable for digital garden.

Avatar `` `src` URLs point to third-party domains (Mastodon, micro.blog, personal blogs) but are loaded by the browser at page-view time — these are NOT site-controlled fetches and don't require CSP `connect-src`; only `img-src` (already permissive at `'self' data: https:`).

github_secrets.note: NO GitHub Secrets consumed in this story. `WEBMENTION_IO_TOKEN` (stored by Story 2.3) is server-side only — used by Story 3.2's daily fetch script, NOT by Hugo templates. This story is purely template + SCSS + fixture-data work.

data_files.file: Schema per architecture lines 871-902. Top level: object keyed by article permalink (with trailing slash). Per-entry fields: type/author/author_url/author_photo/content/url/published. Until Story 3.2 lands, file is absent and `| default (slice)` resolves to empty slice → empty-state path renders for all articles in production.

constraints.constraint: ALWAYS use `| default (slice)` on `index .Site.Data.webmentions_by_article .RelPermalink`. The data file does NOT exist yet (Story 3.2 creates it; AC #9 fixture is the dev-time stand-in). Without `| default`, the build will fail or render incorrectly for articles missing keys. Strictly followed for BOTH lookups (partial in `webmentions.html` AND count line in `single.html`). (Critical Agent Rule #6; architecture line 769.)

NEVER modify existing card variants (`.is-horizontal`, `.is-log`, `.has-image`, `.is-fixed`). Webmention display is mounted in `single.html` outside the card render flow; no `card.html` partial edits. (Critical Agent Rule #1; architecture line 764.) AC #10 byte-equivalent layout guard explicitly tests this.

Critical Agent Rule #3 says "NEVER commit data/*.json files to main branch". This story creates a deliberate, time-boxed exception via AC #9 fixture file. **Mandatory cleanup before merge:** rename to `.example.json` (Hugo ignores `.example` extension) OR delete OR `.gitignore`. Recommended: `.example.json` (preserves documented sample shape for future devs). Coordination flag: Story 3.2's developer must expect NO `data/webmentions_by_article.json` on main when 3.2 lands. (Architecture line 766; epics line 326 endorses the approach.)

Use `{{ .content }}` (Hugo's default auto-escape), NOT `{{ .content | safeHTML }}`. Webmention reply content is third-party-attacker-controlled (architecture line 1062 + ASR-003). HTML in source renders as literal escaped text — slightly worse UX (links don't render as links inside replies), but bulletproof. Story 3.2 owns server-side HTML sanitization with `sanitize-html` allow-list if reply quality suffers. AC #8 decision documented: option (a) auto-escape.

NEVER use jQuery. (Critical Agent Rule #5.) Not directly relevant — this story has ZERO JavaScript (server-side rendering only). Reinforces "no client wrapper libraries" for the webmention integration.

Place new partials at `layouts/_partials/widgets/webmentions.html` and `layouts/_partials/widgets/webmention-group.html` (project widgets convention — siblings: `series.html`, `pagination.html`, `archive.html`, Story 2.2's `heart-button.html`). Architecture's flat `_partials/webmentions.html` sketch (line 87) is reconciled to widgets/ subdirectory for project-convention consistency — same reconciliation Story 2.2 made. Either resolves via Hugo's partial lookup; widgets/ preferred.

Hugo v0.146+ flat layouts convention — `layouts/baseof.html` and `layouts/single.html` at root. Do NOT create `layouts/_default/baseof.html` or `layouts/_default/single.html`. (Same constraint as Stories 2.1, 2.2, 2.3.)

This story does NOT modify CSP. `config/_default/params.yaml` line 22 `imgsrc: ["'self'", "data:", "https:"]` already permits all HTTPS avatar hosts. Line 29 `connectsrc` already includes `https://webmention.io` (Phase 0 Task 4.0). T12 is a regression check, not a change. If browser console reveals CSP violations on avatars during smoke, document gap and either widen `imgsrc` (1-line) or punt to Epic 9.

NO new npm dependencies. Server-side rendering only. Do NOT add `webmention-client`, `indieweb-utils`, `sanitize-html`, or any wrapper. HTML sanitization (when needed) belongs in Story 3.2's processing pipeline.

All external links inside `.webmention` blocks MUST have `rel="noopener external" target="_blank"`. Hugo's `safeHTML` (NOT used here) does NOT auto-add `rel`/`target` — they must be in the rendered HTML directly. AC #6 verifies via grep. Combined with auto-escape (AC #8), prevents both reverse-tabnabbing and XSS via webmention sender content.

All user-visible strings default to German (project convention — existing strings: "Artikel", "Übersicht", "Serie", "Ähnliche Artikel", "Webmentions"). Section heading `Antworten & Erwähnungen` (overrides epics' English "Replies & Mentions"). Type-group headings: `Antworten / Reposts / Erwähnungen / Likes`. Empty-state: `Noch keine Antworten. Sende einen Webmention!`. Pluralization: `Antwort` (n=1) vs `Antworten` (n!=1). Source link tooltip: `Quelle ansehen`. Anchor title: `Zu den Antworten und Erwähnungen springen`. Same German-override pattern Stories 2.2 and 2.3 used. Document language choice in completion notes.

Webmention display is mounted ONLY on the article single-page (`Type == "articles"`). `layouts/single.html` has branches for `Type == "page"` (lines 2-32) and `Type == "articles"` (lines 34-217); NO `Type == "logs"` branch — logs render only on archive list, not as detail pages (per PRD FR-027 "without detail pages"). Logs are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. If a future story adds log detail pages, that story can lift this partial and mount it there. Document deferral in completion notes.

Type-group order is fixed (epics AC #2 verbatim): Replies → Reposts → Mentions → Likes. Renders in this visual order; empty groups are skipped. Reasoning: replies have highest information value (new content), reposts are amplification, mentions are passing references, likes are minimal-signal acknowledgment. Hardcoded in the parent partial (`with $replies` … `with $likes`); no i18n file in project.

Use `{{ with .author_photo }}…{{ end }}` (NOT `{{ if .author_photo }}…{{ end }}`) to skip avatar emission when missing/empty. webmention.io sends `author_photo: ""` (empty string) for senders without avatars; `with` treats empty string as falsy → no `` emitted. Both empty-string and absent-key paths lead to no `` emit (graceful: no broken ``, no placeholder).

Use Hugo's `dateFormat ":date_long"` for `.published` (matches existing single.html lines 87-91 date style). Site `languageCode: de` produces e.g., `15. November 2025`. If locale produces unexpected English output, fall back to `time.Format "02. January 2006"` with hardcoded German month names.

Count line is gated on `gt (len $mentions) 0` — NOT rendered when zero mentions (avoids meaningless "0 Antworten"). The webmentions section itself IS rendered for all articles (with empty-state when zero) so crawlers/screen-readers see stable page structure.

Both `single.html` count line and `webmentions.html` partial perform `index .Site.Data.webmentions_by_article .RelPermalink`. Hugo evaluates this each time at template render — pure data lookup, no I/O cost (JSON parsed once at site load). Decision: accept duplicate lookup for code locality; do NOT pass `$mentions` from `single.html` to partial as a parameter (would require partial-arg refactor — minor complexity, marginal benefit).
Use Hugo whitespace controls (`{{- … -}}`) on surrounding template lines for clean diff and clean rendered HTML. Same project convention as other partials.
Webmention display is data-file-driven. Do NOT add per-article frontmatter (e.g., `webmentions: …`). Counts and entries come from `data/webmentions_by_article.json` keyed by `.RelPermalink`.

Do NOT edit `content/pages/datenschutz.md`. Story 2.3 already added the `## Webmentions` section. Avatar-privacy disclosure note (third-party domain image loading) is a follow-up for Story 2.5 (Privacy Policy Page broader refresh).

Story 2.1 / 2.3 flagged that `config/production/params.yaml` REPLACES (not extends) `_default` `csp.*` lists. INFO-priority for this story: webmention display is server-side rendered (no runtime fetch); only `imgsrc` matters for browser-loading avatars. If production override's `imgsrc` is restrictive, sender avatars may fail to load on the live site (visual: broken `` icons; console: "Refused to load image"). Verify during post-deploy smoke; if observed, escalate to fix the prod override (NOT this story's responsibility).

tests.standards: Lightweight test strategy matching the 2-day epics estimate. Per docs/2-solutioning/test-design-system.md and the test-layering precedent established by Stories 1.1 and 2.1-2.3 (tests/build/ via node:test, tests/e2e/ via Playwright + axe-core, optional XSS guard test for webmention content), webmention display has a content-rendering surface that is most efficiently verified via DevTools Elements + Hugo build smoke + before/after diff of `public/articles/<post>/index.html`. Primary verification is MANUAL SMOKE (DevTools Elements/Console) on a fixture-targeted article + a non-fixture article (empty-state path). Optional automation: ~10-line node:test build assertion (T13) and ~20-line Playwright XSS test (T14) — only if Story 1.1's `tests/build/` and Playwright infra have landed at implementation time (1.1 currently `ready-for-dev`, NOT landed). Do NOT block on Story 1.1. NO unit tests — Hugo template + SCSS rendering is most efficiently verified at the integration level via build output. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `| default (slice)` on data lookup (Critical Agent Rule #6 — non-negotiable). XSS protection is "correct by construction" via Hugo's default auto-escape (AC #8) — Playwright XSS test is verification, not the primary defense.
